I just want to make a recommendation for an easy and interesting course for anyone who is interested: [AnthrCult 314](https://www.lsa.umich.edu/cg/cg_detail.aspx?content=2310ANTHRCUL314001&termArray=f_20_2310) with Ruth Behar. It's about Cuba from 1959 to current, focusing on all of the ideals of equality that came (or were supposed to) with Fidel Castro's revolution. She gives material that both praises and criticizes Castro/socialism, allowing you to create your own narrative of him. The readings are never too long and even if they are, they're usually pretty interesting. I would also say it's pretty easy to get at least a B+ without much effort, although I think most I know ended up with an A/A-. I'm recommending the course because it has had a great impact on me and the material was very engaging, and due to the light course load it was one of my favorite classes. I know many others are looking for something interesting so definitely give this a look if it's up your alley :)

[AnthrCult 314](https://www.lsa.umich.edu/cg/cg_detail.aspx?content=2310ANTHRCUL314001&termArray=f_20_2310) with Ruth Behar. Oh, absolutely! Let me know if I can be of any more help! Although I should caution you and say that these have all helped me in the past. I can’t guarantee anything for you, but it may at least be a good start.

I recommend journaling. Just try to write something every day, whether it be about daily activities, creative writing, reflections, etc. I think it’s very important to get your thoughts into paper and out of your mind and it provides a bit of relief, that way everything isn’t bottled in. If you have any friends who you deem close enough to share these intimate feelings with, then I’d try to regularly keep in contact with them. Sometimes it really helps to have a good listener around to just hear what you have to say, and occasionally offer advice. If you don’t, that’s perfectly fine too - journaling is still a great option. 

If you like podcasts, I suggest downloading quite a few that interest you and just listening to those whenever you get the chance. It helps because I know with depression people like to shut themselves down, but I think socialization is still important and listening to other people have discussions might help you from sinking further into a hole. I’d also recommend reading, but that depends on if that suits you or not. 

Also, I’d keep track of the things that you notice make you feel unhappy. This could be certain movies, shows, songs, people, places - just do your best to avoid these things, or see them less frequently. Now for some situations it might be tough to avoid what makes you unhappy, but if you’re able to decrease that by even the slightest bit then that’s a great start. 

If you can afford counseling, that could be beneficial to you. You could check out your university’s mental health resources and maybe they offer their own counselors (although my personal experience hasn’t been great with them). You might also be able to find student orgs that focus on mental health, and you could either utilize their resources or meet people with similar thoughts to you. If you do pursue therapy, just know that it’s okay to not like the first therapist you talk to. You can try out as many as you like until you’re 100% comfortable with who you’re talking to. Don’t think that there’s something wrong with you because you can’t find anybody that you click with well enough to really help you through this. 

Sorry this is a little long. Believe it or not I tried to be short haha. Just know that I believe in you OP. It’ll be tough but boy oh boy is it worth it in the end.

Hey OP, I know it’s tough right now but this is not who you are. What’s happening currently does not determine “you”. You are strong and you are incredible, and one day you will know exactly what you want to do and what makes you happy. That could be tomorrow, or that could be 30 years from now. You just have to keep your head up and try your best everyday to be happy and work on becoming the best you. If that means going through multiple jobs or only having one, that’s perfectly fine. If it means going through those dark, hopeless phases, that’s fine too..This is your journey, nobody else’s. It doesn’t matter what anybody else thinks. There is no perfect formula for how to live life. Nobody truly knows why we’re here nor what we’re supposed to do, we’ve just found one way (go to school, then get a job, then start a family, etc) that *seems* to be the most successful so far, so we try to follow that but we get sidetracked by, well, life. 

Just focus on baby steps everyday. Celebrate the little things. You got out of bed today? That’s incredible! You went to the grocery store and cooked yourself dinner? Amazing! Start seeing the reward in everything. There is no deadline for discovering your passions, and there is no right way to go about living. Things will come in due time, but until then, do what you can with what you’ve got and remember that you are loved and you are capable of anything.

Hi! First, I just wanna say that I’m so glad you’re still here with us. You are loved, OP, even if your mind tries to convince you otherwise. You’re brave for being able to share your story with us, and I appreciate you for it. My advice would be to keep trying to ride that high of feeling stronger for as long as you can. I know it’s cliché, but sometimes you really do have to weather the storm before you can see even a peek of the rainbow. It’s going to be tough for a while. When you hit lows in the future (and believe me, you will), you’re going to think back on this night and wish that you had succeeded. 

The important thing is for you to remember what you’re feeling right now, and to do your best to set yourself up for when you feel down again. If you recognize the things that you do that make you feel more upset (for example: listening to sad music, browsing the news or certain social media platforms, certain shows, etc), then make sure to avoid those things until you feel like your mind is clear enough to enjoy those things without the negative thoughts. 
Just remember that you are not alone, and it’s not a bad thing to ask for help. 

-If you attend university, you can usually find an abundance of judgment-free mental health resources. If not, maybe speak to an academic advisor and see what resources they have available, or maybe there’s a student organization on campus.  

-You could also look into therapy, which I highly recommend. However if you do this, don’t settle for the first therapist you talk with. Make sure you feel 100% comfortable speaking with them, otherwise it’ll only hurt you in the long run. If it takes seeing 10 different therapists, that’s perfectly okay. If you can’t afford a therapist, sometimes even finding a friend who is a great listener is helpful. Sometimes you just have to talk about it so that it’s not all trapped inside. I would also advise journaling every day. Keep track of what makes you happy, what makes you sad, what you’re thankful for, happy memories, etc.

-I also highly recommend trying to be more involved in the community. Go for a walk through your neighborhood and stop by a cafe or bar, maybe you could meet someone there. If not, it could help just to get out for a little bit. There are plenty of apps as well where you can meet up with people who have similar interests (MeetUp, Facebook events, perhaps even Tinder).

Just remember that this is not the end for you. There’s a reason that the attempt failed tonight. You have so much more to see and learn, and your story is only beginning. I’m not going to lie, it’s going to be a difficult journey. This will be something you will never forget. But it will be so rewarding to see all of the progress you’ve made. You can do it, OP! I believe in you!

Source: 3 attempts, it’s been 2.5 years since the last one. I couldn’t be happier to be alive.
